statement: Samsung and SK Hynix are shifting their primary HBM4 configuration for NVIDIA to 8-high and cutting 12-high output in the second half of 2026, on thermal and stacking-yield grounds.
why: If the tallest HBM stacks cannot be yielded or cooled at volume, memory capacity per accelerator is capped and the memory supply chain for the top platform changes.

impact.mechanism: Retreating from 12-high to 8-high stacks lowers memory capacity per accelerator and signals that stacking, bonding, and packaging yields constrain HBM4 supply.

evidence.excerpt: Samsung and SK Hynix are increasing shipments of HBM4 8-high (8-stack) memory to NVIDIA while reducing 12-high output.

confidence.basis: Secondary only: one fetched Korean outlet citing an unnamed industry source; a consistent second headline was noted but not fetched.
